Omicidx DuckDB Client (R6)

Source: R/omicidx_client.R
OmicidxClient.Rd

Omicidx DuckDB Client (R6)

Omicidx DuckDB Client (R6)

Details

This is the main class for interacting with the OmicIDX data resource. It provides methods for connecting to the Omicidx DuckDB database, listing tables, retrieving dplyr table references, and executing SQL queries.

The OmicidxClient class uses R6 to encapsulate the functionality for connecting to and querying the Omicidx DuckDB database. It provides a user-friendly interface for accessing the data stored in the database.

A typical workflow will involve:

  • Creating a new OmicidxClient object using OmicidxClient$new().

  • Listing available tables using list_tables().

  • Accessing specific tables using tbl() or by referencing tables in the tbls field.

If you need to execute custom SQL queries, you can use the query() method.

The underlying DuckDB database is actually stored on an S3-compatible object store, but the client abstracts away the details of connecting to the database. The database does not need to be downloaded locally; the data are also stored in the cloud and queried remotely via DuckDB.

If you want to persist the DuckDB instance locally (e.g., to cache query results), you can provide a local file path when creating the OmicidxClient object.

Public fields

con

A DuckDB connection object.

tbls

A named list of lazy dplyr table references. Populated during initialization using OmicidxClient$table_names() and OmicidxClient$tbl().

Examples

oidx <- OmicidxClient$new()
#> Error in loadNamespace(x): there is no package called ‘dbplyr’
oidx$list_tables()
#> Error: object 'oidx' not found
# tbl_ref <- oidx$tbl("some_table")
# oidx$query("SELECT * FROM some_table LIMIT 5")

# Get all table names
oidx$table_names()
#> Error: object 'oidx' not found

# Get a description of a specific table
# This is the table "schema"
oidx$describe_table("sources.v_src_sra_studies")
#> Error: object 'oidx' not found

# create a table of SRA runs published per year
runs_by_year <- oidx$tbls$sources.v_src_sra_accessions |>
 dplyr::filter(Type == "RUN") |>
 dplyr::mutate(Year = dplyr::sql("EXTRACT(YEAR FROM Published)")) |>
 dplyr::group_by(Year) |>
 dplyr::summarise(RunCount = dplyr::n())
#> Error: object 'oidx' not found
